name: Cryptography
boundaries: Cryptography: fundamental discoveries and enabling technologies within this field. Include cross-field consequences where the central advance belongs to this field; exclude routine incremental optimization. Use the historical breakthroughs in the prompt to calibrate revolutionary impact.

original_dispositions.original_title: Practical fully homomorphic encryption with polylogarithmic overhead
original_dispositions.reason: The cost revolution is the same concept. Polylogarithmic slowdown is named in CRY-04’s completion as a sufficient form of the proposed demonstration.

original_dispositions.original_title: Provably secure, efficient post-quantum public-key cryptography with keys and speed like elliptic curves
original_dispositions.reason: Deployable post-quantum key encapsulation already exists: FIPS 203 says ML-KEM is believed secure against quantum computers and specifies three parameter sets. The unproved-hardness part is CRY-10. Matching elliptic-curve sizes and speeds, once a standard already runs, is incremental. SQIsign size figures came from specification tables returned in search, not a freshly opened PDF; later tables differ by tens of bytes.

original_dispositions.original_title: Provably secure general-purpose program obfuscation from standard assumptions
original_dispositions.reason: Classical feasibility from well-founded assumptions is achieved and impractical. Post-quantum practicality is the remaining identity of CRY-03.

original_dispositions.original_title: Succinct non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs with constant-size proofs and no trusted setup
original_dispositions.reason: Succinct verifiable computation already exists and is deployed. Constant size without setup would improve concrete proof length and is judged an optimization of an achieved capability. The cited 2025 ePrints concern a soundness warning for a particular transform and standard-model succinct arguments; the full latter paper was not re-read this pass.

original_dispositions.original_title: Information-theoretic multiparty computation with communication independent of the function size
original_dispositions.reason: Honest-majority information-theoretic MPC exists. The cited lower bound conflicts with communication independent of function size for arbitrary functions. Recent near-linear communication belongs in CRY-04’s current state; its revolutionary remainder is concrete cost under computational security.

original_dispositions.original_title: Quantum-secure signatures under 100 bytes with microsecond verification
original_dispositions.reason: FIPS 204 and FIPS 205 already standardize post-quantum signatures. Shrinking an existing signature below 100 bytes is judged incremental. Provable quantum hardness overlaps CRY-10 when the scheme is lattice-based.

Unruh’s cited abstract gives limits on classical everlasting security. Quantum key distribution already gives information-theoretic keys; scaling that channel is judged quantum networking. Certified deletion is narrower and does not by itself protect a classical ciphertext an adversary has stored.

original_dispositions.original_title: Efficient verifiable computation for arbitrary programs
original_dispositions.reason: Outsourced checking with succinct arguments is already a working capability, including post-quantum constructions in the random-oracle model. Information-theoretic succinct proofs are a different and stronger demand; this pass did not find a construction meeting it. Lower prover overhead is judged engineering on an existing tool.

original_dispositions.original_title: A new quantum-resistant assumption that makes indistinguishability obfuscation or functional encryption efficient
original_dispositions.reason: Functional encryption for all circuits is listed by Jain, Lin, and Sahai as a consequence of indistinguishability obfuscation, so a separate entry would split one capability.

original_dispositions.original_title: A Shannon-style master theorem for all quantum-cryptographic possibility
original_dispositions.reason: The wording is a research program, not one missing discovery. Sharp limits already exist for pieces of it. Public unclonable objects and physical position are CRY-05 and CRY-07; a framework settling every remaining question would be a different and vaguer ambition.

reconciliation_change_log.change: 2026-11-01, second pass: kept CRY-01 through CRY-10 and their identities. No concept was deleted, replaced, or merged.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The historical items that looked new were judged to be the same concepts, already-achieved capabilities, incremental size or speed goals, or demands that conflict with proved impossibilities.

reconciliation_change_log.reason: The page records existence as a conjecture, the implication to P ≠ NP, the absence of a known converse, and an explicit universal function that is one-way exactly if any one-way function is.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Tied CRY-02 to the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in computer science. The Impagliazzo–Rudich citation is unchanged from the prior ACM abstract reading.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The list asks both whether one-way functions exist and whether public-key cryptography is possible.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Narrowed CRY-04 against a misreading of information-theoretic MPC with communication independent of the function. Current state records linear-communication progress and completion names the historical polylogarithmic-slowdown target.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Damgård, Li, and Schwartzbach prove an Ω(ng) communication lower bound for some perfectly secure functionalities. The remaining claim is concrete near-plaintext cost, not a new asymptotic existence claim.
